subject: Clarify SOC 2 Type II coverage for Alder Bio — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@alderbio.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@big4audit.com>
Date: 2027-09-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II & bridge letter coverage question for Alder Bio

Hi Kimberly,

Quick one from procurement + our auditor (cc'd). We're starting a vendor review and need to confirm what your most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers for the period ending 2026-12-31. Specifically:

- Does the report explicitly cover requests served from Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) that Alder used in production during the audit period?
- Does coverage extend to customer VPC/private deployments (Alder is evaluating a VPC connector trial)? If not, can Redwood provide a bridge letter or attestation covering private/VPC deployments for the same period?

Our external auditor (Marta) is asking whether any routing/fallback to hosted API endpoints occurred during the period — if so, we may need evidence mapping. Please also indicate the expected timeline for receiving the SOC 2 PDF and any bridge letter draft.

Procurement has a deadline of Oct 6 to complete risk sign-off; auditor deadline is Sept 30 if possible.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Park
Head of Compliance
Alder Bio
helen.park@alderbio.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@alderbio.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II & bridge letter coverage question for Alder Bio

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear ask and for looping Marta in. 

Short answer up front: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report PDF and we will draft a bridge letter clarifying hosting-mode applicability, but the exact wording depends on the environments Alder actually used during the audit window and any routing fallbacks in your traffic. High-level guidance:

- Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending 2026-12-31 covers our hosted API and Redwood Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) operated by Redwood within the reported control environment. If Alder used Dedicated capacity during the audit period and tenant mapping/instance assignment occurred, those Dedicated-hosted nodes are in scope.
- Private/VPC/on-prem deployments are not automatically covered by our hosted SOC 2 report because customers manage network endpoints and some control boundaries. For VPC/private we can provide a bridge letter that: (a) confirms which Redwood control obligations apply to the customer-managed deployment, (b) lists controls not covered, and (c) references the artifacts we can provide (SOC report, configuration screenshots, routing logs summary).

What we need from Alder to finalize the bridge letter:
1) List of deployment modes you used during the audit period (Hosted API, Dedicated pool IDs, VPC connector IDs).
2) Any timeframe where requests routed through hosted endpoints as failover/burst.
3) Target deadline for finalized artifacts.

Operationally we can turn around an initial scope matrix (hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx) within 48–72 hours and a bridge letter draft within 5 business days, assuming you provide the deployment list. We will redact any sensitive tokens; auditors typically accept aggregated logs and tenant mapping screenshots instead of raw tokens.

I'll ask Sean (security) to provide a suggested bridge language and evidence checklist — cc'd. Marissa from Sales is on this for procurement/timeline coordination.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments requested: hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx (please fill and return)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@alderbio.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-28T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II & bridge letter coverage question for Alder Bio

Hi all — Sean from Security. Following up with concrete guidance and a draft bridge text for consideration.

A few clarifications before we finalize wording:
- "Redwood Dedicated" (reserved pools) are in scope of the SOC 2 Type II report when the customer's tenant was assigned to our Dedicated pool during the audit window and tenant isolation controls were in place. We can provide Dedicated pool IDs and the tenant assignment log as evidence.
- "Hosted API" is covered by the report; any request served directly by the hosted API is covered under our control environment.
- "VPC / private" deployments are customer-managed endpoints. We can attest to the runtime software version, the configuration manifest we shipped, and the controls we provide (e.g., KMS integration), but we cannot claim SOC 2 coverage over the customer's network controls. The bridge letter will explicitly state these boundaries.

Suggested bridge letter excerpt (draft):
"During the period 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, Redwood Inference's SOC 2 Type II examination covered the Redwood control environment for hosted and Dedicated (Redwood-operated) inference capacity. For customer-managed VPC/private deployments, Redwood's responsibilities are limited to the software components and service configurations provided by Redwood; network and customer-side controls remain the responsibility of the customer. Evidence available on request includes tenant assignment logs, configuration manifests, and redacted routing summaries."

Evidence we can attach (stubs):
- hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx (filled by Redwood)
- soc2-typeii-2026-report.pdf (redacted cover + attestation page)
- tenant-assignment-log.csv (redacted)
- routing-summary-2026Q4.txt (aggregated counts; no tokens)

Timeline: If Helen provides the list of environments and any routing fallback windows by EOD 2027-09-28, we will circulate a bridge-letter draft by 2027-09-30 EOD.

Happy to have Marta review the exact language; cutting and pasting will likely require small edits for audit wording.

–Sean
Sean Gallagher
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachments included (internal): bridge-draft-redwood.txt (draft), hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx (internal fill)

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@big4audit.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen.park@alderbio.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II & bridge letter coverage question for Alder Bio

Kimberly/Helen — thanks for the context. A couple of auditor-side asks to be explicit about in the bridge: 

1) Please clearly enumerate the components and hosting modes that are in-scope for the 2026 audit period (e.g., Hosted API endpoints in us-west-2, Dedicated pool IDs X/Y between 2026-05-01 and 2026-12-31).
2) If routing fallback to hosted occurred for any Alder traffic, we need either the redacted routing summary or confirmation that fallback did not occur.
3) Token-level artifacts are not required; we will accept tenant assignment logs and aggregated request counts for sampling, but the redaction must ensure no PII or secrets.

We have a hard cutoff for initial artifact intake of 2027-09-30 17:00 to proceed with our planned Q4 testing. If Redwood can provide the bridge draft and the hosting-scope-matrix by then, we should be able to incorporate it. Otherwise, Alder's procurement team may need to accept residual risk.

I can review and provide minor language edits — please send the draft to me and cc Helen.

Regards,
Marta Lopez
Senior Manager, IT Audit
Big4 Audit LLP
marta.lopez@big4audit.com

Attachments: DocuSign link requested for bridge acceptance (placeholder: https://docusign.example/alder/redwood-bridge)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@alderbio.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@big4audit.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II & bridge letter coverage question for Alder Bio

Thanks Marta — we can meet that intake cutoff. Next steps and deliverables from Redwood:

1) We will deliver a completed hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx that enumerates observed deployment modes and any routing fallbacks (expected delivery: 2027-09-30 12:00 PM PT).
2) Draft bridge letter (bridge-draft-redwood.txt) — target 2027-09-30 EOD. Draft will include the suggested excerpt Sean provided and explicit listing of Dedicated pool IDs and hosted regions.
3) SOC 2 Type II PDF (soc2-typeii-2026-report.pdf) — we will provide the attestation page and cover; full report access will be via secure evidence folder link (redwood.app/drive/alder/ALDER-2027-01-evidence).
4) Tenant assignment logs and aggregated routing summary will be uploaded as redacted stubs to the same evidence folder. We will not provide raw tokens.

Marissa will follow up with procurement on DocuSign logistics and any billing/contract notes. Helen — please confirm the list of environments (or attach your completed matrix) so we can finalize.

Thanks — we appreciate the fast turnaround on your side.

Best regards,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: hosting-scope-matrix.xlsx (to be filled), bridge-draft-redwood.txt (draft to follow), soc2-typeii-2026-report.pdf (attestation page)
